candidates.statement: How marketing authorisation holders should inform MHRA of a signal or an ADR to a medicine.
Marketing authorisation holders (MAHs) must send all UK individual case safety reports (ICSRs) and serious non-UK ICSRs directly to MHRA via either ICSR Submissions or Gateway.
candidates.context: For cases in respect to Northern Ireland, use the country code XI to send ICSRs to MHRA.

candidates.statement: Those wishing to report to MHRA need to register with MHRA. Follow the guidance on registering to make submissions to MHRA.
candidates.context: MHRA accepts E2B R2 and R3 format XMLs and will convert E2B R3 cases to E2B R2 for processing into the database. MHRA will transmit Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) reports received directly to the relevant MAH. This will be decided using the suspect drug in the report.

candidates.statement: You do not need to make any changes to your application programming interface (API) connection to our systems. You do not need to inform us that your organisation is R3 ready.
candidates.context: The gateway will continue to accept R2 and R3 XMLs both for ICSRs and acknowledgements. ASPRs will be sent as individual files rather than in batches.

candidates.statement: We will not publish a literature monitoring list. Instead, MAHs will be responsible for conducting relevant literature searches and sending these to MHRA. These should include reports received from the EMA Medical Literature Monitoring (MLM) service. Email [official contact omitted; consult source] if you have any queries on reporting new literature for ADRs.

In line with GVP IX requirements, you should use the Standalone signal notification form (MS Word Document, 132 KB) to send standalone notifications of signals to [official contact omitted; consult source].
candidates.context: A safety signal is information on a new or known adverse event that may be caused by a medicine and requires further investigation. MHRA is responsible for detecting and managing safety signals in regards to UK products. When an MAH becomes aware of an emerging safety issue, they should notify it in writing to MHRA ([official contact omitted; consult source]). For guidance on emerging safety issues, see GVP IX.
